newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Aneka says 1996 net down 30 percent.
newsitem.headline: Aneka says 1996 net down 30 percent.

text.p: Indonesian chemical firm PT Aneka Kimia Raya said on Thursday it estimated its 1996 net profit to drop by 30 percent from 27.74 billion rupiah in 1995.

"We managed to improve our sales last year, but business was difficult, that's why we estimate a 30-percent loss in net profit," Aneka president-director Haryanto Adikusumo told reporters after a shareholders' meeting.
Haryanto, however, said he expected Aneka to improve earnings in 1997, but did not elaborate.
Haryanto also said the company's shareholders approved on Thursday a proposed increase in Aneka's authorised capital to 416 billion rupiah from 250 billion rupiah.
The change in the company's authorised capital was in line with government regulations, Haryanto said.
Haryanto declined to comment on market talk that Aneka was expected to merge with tapioca starch-based sorbitol maker PT Sorbitol Inti Murni Corporation (Sorini).
